text:
Sam: Heads-up — we need a quick decision on candidate fanout defaults for the rerank endpoint. Customer X is hitting 500 candidates and blowing quota + p99 latency.
Anita: Do we have telemetry showing how cost scales with candidate count? IIRC the unit billing is per-score, so 500 -> 500 score units.
Kai: Yep, metrics exist. Quick numbers: median cost per candidate ~0.002 tokens-equivalent, but p99 latency spikes after ~200 due to KV cache churn and batching inefficiencies.
Olivia: Suggestion: console should expose two knobs — `max_candidates` (hard limit) and `sampling_threshold` (soft threshold + sampling policy). Defaults: 200 hard, 300 soft with probabilistic sampling to 200.
Ben: Agreed on knobs. UX note: when you change `sampling_threshold`, show estimated cost delta and p99 latency impact in the modal. Otherwise teams will just toggle blindly.
Sam: Important: models produce scores on different scales. We need a normalization contract so dashboards and A/B rollouts compare apples-to-apples. Options: min-max per-request, z-score using historical mean/std, or a signed logit scale.
Anita: Prefer storing raw scores and a "score_norm" tag in telemetry. E.g., rerank.score_norm="minmax" and expose both raw and normalized in the dashboard. That keeps raw provenance.
Kai: If we add normalization server-side, we need deterministic behavior for canary rollouts. Also document fallback if model doesn't support confidence output.
Olivia: UX for rollouts: allow per-route override of `max_candidates` + model affinity. Example: route canary A uses model-v2 with `max_candidates=150`, fallback to model-v1 with 300.
Sam: We also need to define quota math in docs. Proposal: charge = sum_over_candidates(weight(candidate) * model_unit), where weight defaults to 1, model_unit varies by model class. So 500 cheap-candidates on a tiny model != 500 on a big model.
Ben: Implementation detail: expose `estimated_units` in the API response header `X-Redwood-Estimated-Units: 123`. Console should show this pre-rollout when you load a route config.
Anita: For telemetry naming, propose: `rerank.request.candidates_sent`, `rerank.response.candidates_returned`, `rerank.model.{model_name}.latency.p50|p95|p99`, `rerank.score.norm.{method}`.
Sam: Edge case: downstream services sometimes expect top-k returned but UI calls with huge fanout for recall. We should add a recommended envelope: always include `requested_top_k` and `returned_top_k` in logs.
Kai: Can we add a small API change without breaking existing clients? Idea: optional `client_hints.max_acceptable_latency_ms` and server can apply routing to cheaper models if latency tolerance is low.
Olivia: Love that. Console could surface a slider for SLA per route and preview which models will be used at each SLA tier.
Ben: One more: telemetry for backpressure events. `rerank.backpressure.triggered` with labels {reason: "quota"|"latency"|"memory"} and `rerank.fanout.sample_rate` for sampling decisions.
Sam: Action items: (1) Docs: quota formula + examples (Anita), (2) Console: add `max_candidates` & `sampling_threshold` + cost preview (Olivia), (3) Runtime: emit normalization tags + estimated units header (Kai), (4) Telemetry: implement metric names and backpressure events (Ben).
Anita: I'll draft the docs and include a matrix of costs (model small/medium/large x candidate counts). Putting it in the product doc.
Kai: I'll add the header and normalization tag in the next infra sprint. Will add unit tests proving deterministic normalization.
Olivia: I'll mock the console flows — modal UI + cost graph + SLA slider. Want to run a UX quickloop tomorrow.
Ben: I'll wire up the dashboards and add alerting on `rerank.model.*.latency.p99 > threshold` and on `rerank.backpressure.triggered` spikes.
deploy-bot: Deployed rerank-metrics feature branch to staging at 1718600200 :rocket:
Sam: Nice. Once staging metrics look sane, we can run a small canary with Customer X to validate cost estimation.
Anita: FYI — customer X says they can tolerate up to 250 candidates if p99 < 500ms. We'll use that as the canary config.
Sam: Great. Let's sync in #eng-oncall if we see any surprise backpressure spikes. cc @Olivia for UX follow-up.
